newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - AMLC Beef Weekly - Australian export prices.

text.p: Australian Meat and Livestock Corp's (AMLC) weekly export prices are as follows:
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO U.S. IN U.S. CENTS/LB, CIF.
Bull (95 Chemical Lean) 93 +1 on last week

Chucks (85 CL) 77 +1
AUSTRALIAN EXPORT PRICES TO JAPAN IN U.S. CENTS/LB CIF.
Chilled grassfed fullsets 148 +6 on last week
Chilled grassfed loin:striploin 245 +5

AMLC COMMENTARY: Cattle prices rose this week in Australia's eastern states but were lower in Western and South Australia.
Lamb markets continued the weaker trend evident since the beginning of spring.

Since mid-August, cattle prices in Queensland and Victoria have risen by 10 cents-20 cents a kg. At Toowoomba, Queensland this week bullocks meeting Japan market specifications sold at 20 cents a kg higher than mid-August at 190 cents a kg, while medium-weight cows sold for 142 cents a kg and Korean steers sold for 184 cents a kg, both also up by 20 cents a kg on mid-August. Young cattle of less than 200 kgs sold about 15
cents a kg higher than mid-August at almost A$2.00 a kg.
The Queensland cattle market index this week rose past 100 points for the first time since mid-February, down from 130 at the opening of the year but up from 75 points in April.
In Victoria, over the hooks quotas have risen by 10 cents-15 cents since mid-August.

Extensive areas of Queendsland and New South Wales received rain this week in a good start to the season. Wet weather restricted supplies and encouraged restocker demand, with some works in Queensland finding difficulty sourcing cattle.

Demand from Japan has also increased, although from low levels. Australian chilled grassfed fullsets sold on Japanese wholesale markets this week for 645 yen a kg, their highest level for the year and 200 yen a kg higher than late August. Export prices for fullsets this week rose by 14 cents a kg to 370 cents a kg, 85 cents a kg higher than mid-August but still 83 cents a kg lower than their 1995 average.

Recent price increases in Japan follow declining concern over E. Coli as winter approaches. They also result from tighter supplies of U.S. grainfed beef. As seasonal demand increases supplies in Japan are short, pushing prices higher. Export
levels to Japan, however, are still low.
Also supporting prices, Korean tenders have been announced since mid-August, with the latest the first for the 1997 quota year.

The U.S. market for lean imported grinding beef was slightly higher this week, by 1 cents-3 cents a kg. The firmness is being influenced by tighter supplies of market ready cattle from U.S. feedlots. Since mid-August, U.S. beef production has been consistently below 1995 levels, with production for the past seven weeks 8.4 percent below the correspondinmg period in 1995.
Lamb markets this week were influenced by much higher yardings in Victoria. Export demand for lambs remains firm.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
